speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Do not set your sleeve by the pot-hook, Master Shakespeare. The galls have been on the boil since nine, and copperas never washed out of murrey wool yet.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I smelled it halfway up the stair. Monday has a stout breath.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: A stout breath makes a fast black. Sit. The broth has its fat on it.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: I stirred the gum in twice with the flat stick, mistress, and the hearth-stone is clean.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Your apron is not. Set the bread-board down.

speaker: gillis_verbeke
text: Good morrow, Mistress Ansell. The street is warm, and the kitchen smells of the dyers.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: It smells of honest ink, Master Gillis, not of a ditch. Sit, both of you.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: A finger and a half short of the notch, Mistress?

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: A finger and a half to the hair, and a penny paid at the bakehouse door. The baker looks at the sky when he hands it over.

speaker: gillis_verbeke
text: My master's wife in Norton Folgate said the same loaf was dear, and she did not weigh it in front of me. When the scolding stops, the meal is truly dear.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: I have not stopped. I save Mondays for the copper. He gets the rest of my breath another day.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: You were in before the bar last night, sir. Mistress had it in her hand, and you were already on the stair.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: And sober, though he sat with Will Kemp and Tom Nashe. I set that down to Alice's house, not to mine.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Set it down to her paper. Two shillings and eightpence, and the jug. I did not divide it, and I am not dividing it at this table.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: And what did the evening teach you that my table does not sell at threepence?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: That a salt-fish may belong to two authors before the bill comes, and that neither of them owns the jug.

speaker: gillis_verbeke
text: That is a pattern-book. One man draws the leaf, another turns the stem, and the master sells the yard.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Do you play this afternoon, sir?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Titus, at two. An old Roman. I am dead by the fourth act, and I do not come on again.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Then be dead tidy, and be home before my ceiling learns a new trade. Tomorrow morning is yours, if you mean to use it on a king and not on my tallow.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Tomorrow morning is the king. This afternoon is the Roman.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: I will leave the fresh horn by the basin when the copper is strained.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The old horn will do. There is black in the bottom of it.

speaker: gillis_verbeke
text: A morning window is cheaper than two candles, and kinder to the eyes.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Eat. Threepence on the dresser. Keep your cuff off the ink-pan as you go.
